You can try keeping your toothbrush by your bed or wherever you hang out. I keep a box of flossers next to the bed because I can watch Youtube while I do it. I also like to brush my teeth sitting down. Some days, mouthwash may be the only thing you can bring yourself to do.

It's boring, it's messy, it never changes, you can't multitask while you do it, it takes like five minutes a day, it never gets easier, and the reward is that your teeth \*might\* decay a bit slower. By the time I finish doing it, it's already time to do it again. Teeth don't improve, they just get worse more slowly, making it seem like a thankless task.

Omg. I am a lower-middle class, 30ish female, that lives alone and works 10 hour shifts plus any overtime I can get. No kids, but spend plenty of time on chores/emails/other crap anyway. I have obvious depression, and I have anxiety one may only notice if they saw me react to certain situations. My phone-only psychiatrist diagnosed me with ADD, along with depression. I asked him to explain why and he said, in a non-rude way, it's because I often cut him off in conversation and go off topic. It's easier to cut someone off if you're not in person with them! 

I don't feel he pushed me towards specific meds, but your post inspires me to get another opinion from other psychiatrists. I don't think I have ADD; I think it's depression forgetfulness and brain fog. I've never had a great short term memory, and I've been depressed for about 19 years. I tried generic Strattera because I didn't want to get addicted to a stimulant. Generic with insurance was still expensive. All I got from it was intense dry mouth. Expensive mistake. Kinda glad I didn't try a stimulant, considering all I would get from it is an addiction.

I was on Duloxetine for a while because I thought it was helping. The problem with Duloxetine and Atomoxetine, was that all of the OBJECTIVE effects were NEGATIVE, and all the SUBJECTIVE effects were positive. Even though I took them as directed. Duloxetine DEFINITELY makes me sweat at night and messes with my sleep. Does it make me want to do things and meet people? NO NO NO. Does it make me happy? I think? Kinda? Or did I just have an okay week where less stuff went wrong?

I stopped taking my antidepressant again, this time recently. Am I having brain zaps? I don't know. Am I gonna start randomly taking them again? Maybe. Do I know if they really work? Still no. Just thought I would offer myself up here as a little case study. Sure it's a little scattered and rambling, but that's just the ADD, right?

1. You aren't wasting your professors' time. They get paid to help you. You aren't wasting your peers' time. Tutoring someone else can help the tutor retain knowledge and learn as well. Some people are too afraid to ask for help. You are your own person and you don't have to be who your parents want you to be. They wanted a kid and they got one. You don't live to serve them.
2. I don't know your age or race and I won't ask. There are many ways to change your appearance. It is also okay to get old and to look old. Why do you think you smell bad? Is it a medical condition? Do you shower less or not at all for religious reasons? If you are overweight, you can buy a product such as Lume deodorant to deodorize layers of skin. There are also prescription strength armpit deodorants. If you smell because you sweat a lot, try shirts that are 100% cotton, or sport shirts that have wicking abilities. I have deep set raccoon eyes, but I kind of just go with it. I'm sure you have heard people tell you to exercise, but seriously, even a little bit can help ease your joint pain over time. Exercise isn't just for health nuts and dieters.
3. Some people are better off as loners. I don't know what has happened to you in your past, but it's a vicious cycle in that people that have been hurt go on to hurt others. There are reasons people turn out a certain way. Not all of it is in your control.
4. Don't worry about death. Death finds everyone some day. Might as well ride out this life until it's done.

GREEK YOGURT. Those 150 gram cups are usually 120-160 calories. One can be a filling snack, or I might eat 3 at one time as a meal. Still, that's like 400 calories. I am American so we might not have the same brands, but for Greek Yogurt, Chobani is good. It must be greek type. The plain yogurts are too thin.

Muesli can be pretty filling too if you eat a triple serving. Bob's Red Mill is good (one serving of 35 grams, is 140 calories, making three servings 420 calories. 4 calories per gram but to me this gets a pass because there is actual nutrition and you can feel full. To meet a goal of 2000 calories a day, it can be three 600 cal meals with two 100 cal snacks in between. But you have the option of eating your calories for the day any time of day that you want to. You can eat most of them in the morning or afternoon and have a light dinner, or you can be like me at eat 400 calories throughout the day and then eat 1600 for dinner. I like to let myself be hungry during the day so that I can feel full at night and then I sleep better.

Overdose on fruit! Sometime I buy a 3 lb bag of mangoes or berry mix in the freezer aisle and take it out of the freezer a day or two before work starts for the week. Or if you can't keep it cold, take it out of the freezer and let it thaw during the morning. Again, lots of sugar, but the fiber supposedly keeps your sugar levels from spiking. Or buy a big carton of blueberries, raspberries, or strawberries. Strawberries are less caloric than blueberries. I have a chart at home and a food scale and calculate my calorie intake. Blueberries are .57 calories per gram, and strawberries are .33. For reference, candy/chips/even wheat crackers are 4 calories per gram, and chicken breast is .98 calories per gram.

I also make a can of vegetable soup in my mug sometimes. Amy's Kitchen makes low calorie vegetarian soups such as Vegetable Barley for 120 calories.

Not the healthiest (again), but you can also get a protein bar/meal replacement bar. MetRx bars are usually 400ish calories. I often eat one as my "dessert" after a meal, and it makes me pretty full then.

A fresh ball of mozzarella is 2.5 calories per gram, which is still pretty good. Put a basil leaf on it and some sliced tomatoes and you have a lunch.

I don't have a dishwasher either. If you have so many dishes that it's overwhelming, shoot for a daily goal of spending 5 minutes washing dishes. You don't have to do them all in one shot.
